def test_closest_integer():
    # Basic integers (no decimal point)
    assert closest_integer("10") == 10
    assert closest_integer("-10") == -10
    assert closest_integer("0") == 0
    assert closest_integer("5") == 5

    # Regular rounding (not a .5 tie)
    assert closest_integer("15.3") == 15
    assert closest_integer("15.7") == 16
    assert closest_integer("-15.3") == -15
    assert closest_integer("-15.7") == -16
    assert closest_integer("123.456") == 123

    # .5 ties round away from zero
    assert closest_integer("14.5") == 15
    assert closest_integer("-14.5") == -15
    assert closest_integer("0.5") == 1
    assert closest_integer("-0.5") == -1
    assert closest_integer(".5") == 1
    assert closest_integer("-.5") == -1
    assert closest_integer("999.5") == 1000
    assert closest_integer("-999.5") == -1000
    assert closest_integer("123456789.5") == 123456790

    # Trailing zeros are stripped before the '.5' check
    assert closest_integer("10.50") == 11
    assert closest_integer("-10.50") == -11
    assert closest_integer("2.500") == 3
    assert closest_integer("-2.500") == -3
    assert closest_integer(".500") == 1
    assert closest_integer("10.00") == 10
    assert closest_integer("0.0") == 0

    # Values that reduce to whole numbers after stripping zeros
    assert closest_integer("1.0") == 1
    assert closest_integer("-1.0") == -1
    assert closest_integer("100.000") == 100
    assert closest_integer("-100.000") == -100

    # Empty string is not a valid float
    try:
        closest_integer("")
        assert False, "expected ValueError for empty string"
    except ValueError:
        pass
